notebook: Fainted Pokemon stay fainted until a pokecenter (+). My Bulbasaur died leading into a Fire trainer at Lv7. ALWAYS check trainer type tooltip and set_lead a counter BEFORE entering; if no counter exists, take XP fights deliberately or skip.
Kanto starters: Bulbasaur 19HP/11SpA Magical Leaf 40; Charmander frail 18HP Incinerate 60; Squirtle balanced Bubble. Bulbasaur's bulk+Grass coverage is safest pick.

Type-advantage leads can still faint: my Lv40 Venusaur (Leftovers) died at 0 HP vs a Poison Grunt. Never enter a trainer with the lead already damaged; heal at + BEFORE it gets low, and keep a healthy backup lead.

"Various" trainers are NOT safe XP: an Ace Trainer on map 5 fainted 5 of my 6 (Lv41-48) Pokemon in one fight. Treat unreadable-type trainers as boss-level threats — skip them when low on HP or near a gym, or lead the bulkiest counter you have, never assume neutral bulk suffices.

Map 1 step 18: led Lv10 Bulbasaur (Energy Ball 90 STAB SE) vs "Bug Catcher — Bug" and it STILL fainted Bulbasaur AND Eevee (Lv9). Type advantage at low levels does not guarantee wins here — expect ~2 levels above you per trainer tier. Do not enter trainers with only 2-3 bodies; keep everyone healed, not just the lead.

Map 0 step 10: Lv11 Bulbasaur (Assault Vest, SE STAB Grass) FAINTED vs "Fisherman — +2 Levels — Water". Type advantage is NOT enough at low level; trainers run ~+2 levels over you. Don't lead a damaged or underlevelled mon into any trainer; prefer pokecenter/Sacred Ash first.

Map 1 step 17: led Lv11 Growlithe (Fire resist) vs "Officer — +2 Levels — Fire" and BOTH Growlithe and Voltorb fainted. Resistance alone does not save you at low level — trainers here hit far above their level. Only enter trainers with a SE STAB lead AT or ABOVE their level, and never with your only counter.

Map 1 step 18: Lv11 Sandshrew (Bulldoze, SE vs BOTH of Scientist's types, full HP) STILL fainted vs "Scientist +2 Levels". Even perfect type matchup loses ~2 levels down. Rule: do not enter ANY trainer below their level tier; grind wilds/catches first, trainers are boss-tier fights in this game.

Map 0 Kanto: even a WILD fight can faint a low-level lead — my Lv5→6 Bulbasaur hit 0 HP in a +1 level wild battle. Never let your only healthy body lead; check HP after every fight and beeline to the pokecenter (+) when a mon drops low or faints.
Map 1: even +1-level WILD fights can faint my lead — Lv11 Bulbasaur (Miracle Seed) hit 0 HP in one. Wilds are not free XP either; heal at + whenever anyone drops below half.
Kanto map 0 start: trainers run ~+2 levels over you; even SE STAB leads faint ~2 levels down. Grind wilds/catches to trainer level before ANY trainer; heal at + whenever anyone drops below half.
Usable bag items (TM, Rare Candy) are NOT auto-used: my Rare Candy sat unused, Bulbasaur stayed Lv9. Only use them when a "use item" action appears; don't count levels until applied.

Map 2 step 28: my Lv20 Ivysaur (full HP, Expert Belt) FAINTED in a plain +1-level wild battle. Even wilds are lethal here; never take any fight with fewer than 3 healthy bodies, and beeline to + when anyone hits 0.

Map 0 Kanto step 7: Lv9 Bulbasaur FULL HP, SE STAB Grass, RESISTING Poison still FAINTED vs Rocket Grunt +2Lv. Trainers here outscale hard — do not enter ANY trainer until your whole team is at/above their tier AND you have 3+ healthy bodies; leads die even with perfect matchup ~2 levels down.
Leftovers does NOT stop faints at low level: Lv6 Bulbasaur with Leftovers still hit 0 HP in a +1-level wild on map 0. Regen is too slow when outdamaged; heal at + regardless of held item.
Map 0 Kanto: even a FULL-HP Lv5 lead fainted in a +1-level WILD fight (Slowpoke 21HP→0). Wilds are not safe XP below ~Lv7; only take fights with your highest-level mon leading and 3+ bodies.

Kanto map 0 recipe that earned badge 1: stack 4-5 catches early (bodies > levels), take ONE trainer (Rocket Grunt Poison) with a resisting full-HP lead, heal at + right before the gym. Zero faints. Repeat this shape every map.

Kanto map 0 layer-4 Rocket Grunt (+2Lv Poison) has fainted my full-HP Lv7 resisting Grass lead in TWO separate runs. That trainer is stronger than its label: do not enter it before ~Lv9-10, or skip it entirely. The "recipe" of taking one early trainer is NOT safe.
Kanto $ trade: returns a copy 3 levels higher, but does NOT always heal — my fainted Bulbasaur came back Lv15 still at 0/38. Trades are free levels only; a pokecenter (+) is still required to revive.

Kanto map 1: even +1-level WILD fights with full-HP Lv10-11 SE leads fainted Bulbasaur AND Mankey in back-to-back wilds (step 17-18). Wilds here are NOT safe XP below ~Lv12; budget HP per fight and never chain wilds without a + between them.

Map-0 trainers whittled my Lv11 Bulbasaur from full to 0 HP across 2 fights even while resisting (Water/Poison). Trainers hit harder than expected: heal at every pokecenter offered, and don't stack fights on one Pokemon.

Kanto map 1 cleared (badge 2): team of catches (Kabuto/Onix/Dodrio) + starter worked; trainers give +2 levels each and are worth taking over wilds when a type-counter lead exists. Catch nodes early = cheap bodies.
Kanto map 2 gym = Lt. Surge, Electric (Pikachu/Voltorb/Raichu ~Lv20-25): Sandslash Lv27 with Ground STAB swept it at full HP. Ground lead walks Electric gyms. Badge 4.
Wild fights are never free even when winning: my Lv30 Sandslash went full→32/85 on a +1 level wild. Only send a lead into a wild if it resists AND is >60% HP.

DANGER: an Ace Trainer ("Various", map 3 layer 3) took my whole team except one from full to 0 in ONE fight — trainers can spike far above expectations. Never enter a trainer without a full-HP counter-lead AND a healthy backup; "Various" = unknown types = highest-risk node type.

Kanto map 1 Rocket Grunt (Poison) took my Lv15 Bulbasaur AND Lv14 Nidoran-m from full to 0 in one trainer fight — trainers hit far above their level tag. Two faints mid-map with no pokecenter until layer 7. Rule: assume each trainer fight costs ~1 full HP bar even when countering; plan heals accordingly.

Kanto map 1: a trainer fight damages the WHOLE team, not just the lead — my Electric/Poison Scientist fight left 5/6 Pokemon at 0 HP even with a resisting full-HP Magnemite lead. Trainers here are near-full-team-wipe events; never take two trainer nodes in a row without a pokecenter between them.

Map-0 wilds are lethal even with Eviolite: my Lv6 Bulbasaur (Eviolite, resisting?) hit 0 HP on a +1-level wild at n3_0. Wilds here can one-shot a Lv6 lead. Until ~Lv10, avoid ALL fights when possible; only fight with a full-HP bulk lead.
Kanto starters: Bulbasaur Lv5 = bulky Grass/Poison SP.A with Magical Leaf; Charmander frail fast Fire; Squirtle bulky Water. Bulbasaur's bulk suits this game's brutal trainer damage.

Kanto map 0 cleared (badge 1): Bulbasaur/Seel/Drowzee all Lv12-13, no faints. Route that worked: 2 early catches, Scientist(Elec/Poison)->Drowzee, Fisherman(Water)->Seel, Rocket(Poison)->Drowzee, Surf from map-0 move tutor on Seel, pokecenter at layer 7 before gym.

Kanto map1: my Lv16 Ivysaur (Miracle Seed, resisting Poison lead) FAINTED to the layer-3 Rocket Grunt. Trainers can kill even ideal counter-leads; budget ~1 death per trainer pre-pokecenter and never enter one with <3 healthy team members.

Kanto map1 Firebreather (Fire) killed my Lv15 full-HP Bulbasaur DESPITE resisting — map-1 trainers can kill even ideal counter-leads from full. Rule: enter any map-1+ trainer with 3+ healthy bodies and expect the lead to lose its bar.

set_lead is FREE but you MUST call it before play() — in run 3 I planned "Psyduck counters Fire Officer" then never set the lead; Bulbasaur led and fainted 0/23. Always verify slot 0 before any trainer/wild node.

Kanto map 1 trainers kill even FULL-HP ideal counter-leads every time (Bug Catcher killed Lv12 Kabuto Rock-vs-Bug; Firebreather killed resisting Bulbasaur/Psyduck). Trainers here are not "counter and survive" — expect the lead to faint no matter what. Only enter one with 3+ spare bodies AND a revive/heal in hand; otherwise route around via items/catches.

Kanto map1 Bug Catcher killed my Lv13 full-HP Vulpix (Fire STAB super-effective vs Bug). Confirms note 16 absolutely: NO lead survives a map-1 trainer, not even SE STAB counters. Trainers = ~1 faint each, always.

Even a +1-level WILD can kill a full-HP Lv9 counter-lead (my Bulbasaur 25/25 → 0 on map-1 wild). Below ~Lv12, NO fight is safe in Kanto; route catches/items/tutors/trades only until the team is Lv10+.

Kanto map 0 Rocket Grunt (Poison) killed my Lv9 resisting Bulbasaur from full: even map-0 trainers cost ~1 faint. Rule all maps: never enter a trainer with <3 healthy bodies, expect the lead's bar gone.

Kanto map1 Fisherman (Water) vs full-HP Lv14 Horsea lead: Horsea AND Ivysaur AND Onix all hit 0 in one trainer fight; only Geodude survived at ~55%. Confirms notes 16-17: one map-1 trainer ≈ 3 faints, not 1. Route: after ANY trainer, go straight to the next pokecenter before anything else.
Evolution stones go to BAG, not auto-used — no "use" action appears on map screens, so don't plan around evolving unless a use option actually shows up.
Kanto map 1 run 5: route = catch n1_0 → items/catches over trainers until Lv12+ (notes 16-20: one trainer ≈ multiple faints), tutor if offered, pokecenter at layer 7 before gym B8.
Map-0 Firebreather killed my Lv7 Bulbasaur lead from 0 HP bar start? No: it entered at full and hit 0 — even map-0 trainers faint the lead. Confirms notes 16-19 on map 0 too.

Kanto map-1 +1 wilds killed FULL-HP leads: Seel Lv12 (0/37), Onix Lv10 DEF33 (0/27). Fights cost ~1 full bar no matter the bulk/level. Rule: budget one faint per fight node; only fight when you have 3+ spare bodies and a pokecenter ahead.

Move tutor upgraded Bubble→Surf (50→80 STAB) on my lead — huge value in autobattles; prioritize tutor nodes for the lead's STAB every map. Trade node also gave +3 levels to a weak body: both beat fighting an over-levelled trainer early.

Kanto m1: Rocket Grunt (Poison, +2 lvls) KO'd my Lv13 Squirtle leading with Water STAB — a 2-level gap kills even a type-advantaged full-HP lead. Never take a trainer while any healthy body is 2+ levels under; prefer trade/tutor nodes to close gaps first.

Kanto map 1: my Lv18 Geodude with Wide Lens FAINTED to a Rock/Ground Hiker even leading with type advantage — autobattles trade HP hard; don't send a low-level or frail body as lead expecting a clean win, and heal fainted mons at pokecenter (layer 7) before gym.

Autobattles chip leads down fast on long maps: I reached map 7 with Blastoise AND Rhyperior at 0/HP before the pokecenter. Take heal nodes EARLY when a lead drops under ~40%, don't stack wild fights on one lead — rotate set_lead between healthy bodies.

notebook: Kanto map 0: Officer/Firebreather trainers = Fire Pokemon, Water STAB lead walks them. Pokecenter at layer 7 sits right before the gym: take it if lead under ~80% HP. Items do NOT carry between runs — only notes do; re-equip each run.

Red Card does NOT save a badly disadvantaged lead: Kanto map 1 Scientist (Electric/Poison) one-shot my Lv16 Wartortle from full HP. Never let a weak-to-type Pokemon lead a trainer fight — swap lead first, it's free.
Read the gym leader's tooltip as soon as its node is visible — never enter an unscouted gym. Plan the counter-lead several layers ahead so you arrive with the right type and full HP.

Resist ≠ safe: Lv8 Voltorb (Electric, resists Electric) fainted to a +2 Levels Scientist on Kanto map 0. Don't lead an underlevelled mono-resist into a +2 Levels trainer; lead the healthy STAB carry instead.

Move tutor tier upgrades are huge: Bubble→SURF(80), Bulldoze→EARTHQUAKE(100) roughly doubled damage. Take the tutor whenever reachable. Expert Belt on an SE-hitting STAB carry (Squirtle vs Fire map) cleared Kanto map 0 losing zero HP.

Wild battles are NOT free XP: my full-HP Lv22 Krabby fainted to a Kanto map-2 wild node. Check the wild's likely type before leading; never assume a battle node is safe just because it says "+1 level".

Kanto run 2 draft worked well: 5 bodies by map 0's end (catches cost turns, not HP); coverage core = Water lead + Electric + Fighting + Ground/Rock + bulky Water backup. Choice Scarf on the fastest STAB carry = guaranteed first strike every battle, best early item.

Kanto map1 Scientist (+2Lv, Elec/Poison) killed BOTH my leads: Lv10 Geodude was ELECTRIC-IMMUNE and still fainted, then backup died too. Immunity/resist does not protect an underlevelled lead — arrive at +2Lv trainers Lv13+, or skip them entirely.

Map-1 wilds are NOT free XP: they've killed a FULL-HP Surf Squirtle twice AND a full-HP Lv9 Kabuto (run 8). No lead is safe there — treat every map-1 wild as costing a body's worth of HP or worse. Skip wilds whenever a catch/item/question/trade node exists; if forced, lead the most expendable body with healthy backup.

+2Lv trainers: survivable ONLY with FULL-HP on-level SE-STAB lead AND a pokecenter within 1-2 layers after — and even then expect heavy HP loss on maps 1+ (run 20: Officer/Fire took Surf Squirtle from ~full to 8/28). Map-0 single-Pokemon trainers are the only cheap ones. Anything less than full HP + SE lead + heal nearby = skip.

Kanto map 0 cleared to badge 1, zero faints: 3 bodies (Squirtle/Seel/Drowzee), tutor SURF on lead, took every +2Lv trainer with a counter-typed healthy lead. Map 0 trainers are single-Pokemon and safe if you out-type them.

Catches raise your LEVELS too, not just body count: drafting Lv8-10 catches through map 1 lifted my whole team toward the +2Lv-trainer threshold without fighting anything. Prefer the highest-level catch offered over wild XP every time.

Tutors stack within a run: Kanto maps 0-2 offered multiple tutors and I upgraded twice (Bubble→Surf→Hydro Pump on one carry). Always take every reachable tutor; put each upgrade on your strongest STAB carry.

Kanto map 0 clean route (2 runs zero faints): catch->catch->tutor(Surf)->second tutor(EQ)->pokecenter->gym, skipping ALL battles. REVISED run 11: the 'safe wild' step nearly killed my lead (full->3/21) — map-0 wilds are not safe either; skip every battle node on map 0 too.
Evolution EXISTS in Pokelike (run1 Squirtle became Wartortle ~Lv16). Eviolite (+50% DEF/SpD) BLOCKS evolution — great short-term bulk on a lead/carry, but permanent evo lock; weigh before equipping.

Rare Candy HP bug is INTERMITTENT: run 11 candy left lead at full HP, but an earlier run showed 0/34 after a candy with no battle logged. Still check team HP after ANY consumable; if a body shows 0HP, heal or swap lead before any battle node (chain-wipe risk, note 24).

Kanto map 1: pokecenter at layer 7 sits right before the gym (layer 8). Trade nodes appear mid-map (layers 4/6 in earlier runs, layer 5 in run 9) — always scout the offer; they're +3 levels at zero risk.
TM items exist as USABLE move-tier upgrades (same effect as tutors, ~doubled damage): always take over stat items like Scope Lens. Check team HP after using any consumable (note 17 bug risk).

When your team is FULL (6/6), catch nodes become upgrades: pick the highest-level catch that duplicates your weakest body, then release the old one in the swap screen. Run 3: turned Lv9 Tangela into Lv12 free.

Trades DO work: each "+3 levels" trade raised that Pokemon by exactly 3 (run 4: Lv5->8, Lv4->7 x2). I misread the pre-gym screen. Trades are free levels with zero HP risk — take them when offered, prefer trading your lowest-level body.

Kanto map-1 item pools VARY by run: run 16 got Sacred Ash at layer 5, run 17 got only stat items (Eviolite/Expert Belt/Choice Band). Never route-counting on a specific item appearing; treat item nodes as upside. Expert Belt (+100% on SE) onto a Specs+STAB carry is the best of that pool.

Kanto map 0 clean route, 5 runs zero faints incl. this one: catches/trades/items nearly every layer, at most ONE +2Lv trainer with a full-HP bulky lead. Held slots are PER BODY: stack Scarf+Wide Lens+Quick Claw so all three bodies strike first with boosted damage. Tutor both carries (Surf+EQ) before the gym.

Wild battles CHAIN-KILL, worst case run 8: I entered a map-1 wild while my LEAD WAS ALREADY AT 0HP (fainted in the previous wild) — the game auto-sent bodies #2,#3,#4 and ALL fainted; 4 of 5 gone in one node. RULE: read team HP on the map screen before EVERY battle node; if the lead shows 0HP the fight starts with the next body and can wipe you.

Catches vary hugely in stats at the same level: run 7 map-1 pool had Pinsir Lv9 ATK 27 vs Drowzee HP29/SpD21 vs Staryu ~14s. Read the stat line, don't pick by level or shininess alone; a 27-ATK STAB body outlevels its number fast.

Re-check held items after any move upgrade: Metronome's type-flip became redundant once Geodude learned native Ground STAB (Bulldoze) — swapped it for Expert Belt (+100% on SE hits). Item slots are scarce; an item bought for an old moveset can be strictly worse later.

Kanto map1 Hiker (+2Lv, Rock/Ground): my doubled ~480-eff Surf did NOT one-shot — after the fight Squirtle AND Geodude both showed 0/36 and 0/33. A 'perfect counter' +2Lv trainer can still cost two bodies. Check team HP immediately after ANY trainer fight; never assume the calc guarantees a kill.

Opening item doctrine: Choice Specs (+30% special) onto the special STAB carry; King's Rock (30% flinch) onto the FASTEST body — hitting first means flinch erases the enemy's whole turn. Both stack across different Pokemon.

Kanto map 1 clean opening: catch nodes through layers 0-4, then TWO tutors reachable back-to-back (~layers 5-6) — took both over +2Lv trainers (Scientist/Fisherman/Hiker all present, all lethal at Lv<13): Surf on Water lead + Earthquake on Ground/Rock = two full-HP upgraded carries, zero HP lost by layer 6.

Kanto map1 Fisherman (+2Lv Water): full-HP Lv11 Exeggcute RESISTING Water and hitting SE Grass still FAINTED, and the chain killed Psyduck + Rhyhorn too — 3 bodies in one node. +2Lv trainers are run-enders regardless of typing; only enter one if a pokecenter is reachable within 1-2 layers after, and expect to lose the lead even when the matchup is perfect.

Map-1 wilds can kill THREE bodies in ONE node (run 12): full-HP Lv13 Kabuto (Rock/Water, bulkiest body) led and fainted, then Squirtle + Magnemite chained behind it. NO lead survives a map-1 wild, not even a bulky STAB counter. Never enter any map-1 battle node unless the layer has nothing else; if forced, expect to lose the lead and 1-2 more bodies.

Wilds anywhere cost HP: run 21 map-0 +1Lv wild took full-HP Lv6 Squirtle from 21 to 13 (~8 HP), not the ~2 earlier runs saw. Rule stands: never enter a wild hurt or under-levelled; if forced, lead healthiest body with healthy backup behind (chain-wipe risk, note 24). Map-1+ wilds remain near-unenterable.

Check team HP on the map screen IMMEDIATELY after every battle node: run 12's single wild left 3 of 6 bodies at 0HP. If any body shows 0HP, route to a pokecenter before anything else — the layer-7 pokecenter before Kanto map-1 gym saved that run.
Moon Stone = USABLE force-evolution kept in BAG, works at any level (run 13, map 0): evolve the lead carry for a permanent stat jump; check HP after any consumable (note 17 bug risk).
Trades FAIL silently when your team is FULL (6/6): run 14 map-1 trade node consumed the turn, no swap screen appeared, body unchanged. Only enter a trade with an open slot, or expect nothing.
Call set_lead in its OWN turn and wait for "ok", then play(): batching them in one block can fail silently (run 15 step 4) and the intended lead sat behind while Squirtle tanked a wild to half HP.

Trades give +3 LEVELS but never heal (run 16: fainted Drowzee stayed 0/34). WORSE, run 19: right after a trade node, FOUR bodies showed 0/HP with no battle logged — silent HP loss or display bug around non-battle nodes. RULE: re-read the team HP bar on the map screen after EVERY node, battle or not; if the lead shows 0HP, set_lead a living body before any fight and route to a pokecenter ASAP.

Kanto map 0 run 17 clean: catch-heavy route + ONE counter-typed trainer (Officer/Fire vs Water STAB lead) cost only 3 HP total; reached map 1 with 4 full-HP bodies by Lv11. Counter-typed single-Pokemon trainers on map 0 are cheap levels; everything else = catches.

Run 18 Kanto map1 opening worked: catches layers 0-4 (5 bodies), items→Expert Belt(Squirtle)+Specs(Magnemite), one trade, ZERO battles entered = all full HP at layer 5. Check each node's "next:" line before picking — a catch can force your next layer into battle/question while an item keeps safe chains open.

Opening doctrine (any region): draft the bulkiest starter, prefer Water STAB; route catch/item/trade/tutor nodes ONLY, skip every battle node (wilds included) until carries are upgraded; stack held items per-body on STAB carries; heal at any pokecenter before a gym; scout gym tooltip layers ahead.

Silent-loss bug hits QUESTION nodes too (run 22 map1): after a random-event node, Mankey+Squirtle+Exeggcute ALL showed 0HP with no battle logged. Rule stands stronger: re-read team HP bars after EVERY node of ANY type; if lead is 0HP, set_lead a living body same turn and route to pokecenter before anything else.

Pokecenter at layer 7 is mandatory before the gym at layer 8 unless everyone is full. Read the gym tooltip as soon as visible and set the counter lead in its own turn before entering. Re-check team HP after EVERY node (silent-loss bug, notes 37/24).

Red Card does NOT save a badly disadvantaged lead: Kanto map 1 Scientist (Electric/Poison) one-shot my Lv16 Wartortle from full HP. Never let a weak-to-type Pokemon lead a trainer fight — swap lead first, it's free.
Read the gym leader's tooltip as soon as its node is visible — never enter an unscouted gym. Plan the counter-lead several layers ahead so you arrive with the right type and full HP.

Resist ≠ safe: Lv8 Voltorb (Electric, resists Electric) fainted to a +2 Levels Scientist on Kanto map 0. Don't lead an underlevelled mono-resist into a +2 Levels trainer; lead the healthy STAB carry instead.

Move tutor tier upgrades are huge: Bubble→SURF(80), Bulldoze→EARTHQUAKE(100) roughly doubled damage. Take the tutor whenever reachable. Expert Belt on an SE-hitting STAB carry (Squirtle vs Fire map) cleared Kanto map 0 losing zero HP.

Wild battles are NOT free XP: my full-HP Lv22 Krabby fainted to a Kanto map-2 wild node. Check the wild's likely type before leading; never assume a battle node is safe just because it says "+1 level".

Kanto run 2 draft worked well: 5 bodies by map 0's end (catches cost turns, not HP); coverage core = Water lead + Electric + Fighting + Ground/Rock + bulky Water backup. Choice Scarf on the fastest STAB carry = guaranteed first strike every battle, best early item.

Kanto map1 Scientist (+2Lv, Elec/Poison) killed BOTH my leads: Lv10 Geodude was ELECTRIC-IMMUNE and still fainted, then backup died too. Immunity/resist does not protect an underlevelled lead — arrive at +2Lv trainers Lv13+, or skip them entirely.

Kanto map1: a full-HP Lv11 Surf+Leftovers Squirtle FAINTED farming a "+1 level" wild for a single level. Wilds are not safe XP farms even with STAB advantage — treat every battle node as able to take a body. Don't grind wilds for +2Lv-trainer thresholds; arrive via catches/items instead.

+2Lv trainers faint even perfect leads: Kanto map1-2 Bug Catchers killed Lv13 AND Lv15 Flying-STAB leads; map1 Firebreather fainted my Lv13 Surf-STAB Squirtle (super-effective, still died). Enter +2Lv fights expecting to lose the lead's HP or the body; heal immediately after, never enter one with your only healthy carry.

Kanto map 0 cleared to badge 1, zero faints: 3 bodies (Squirtle/Seel/Drowzee), tutor SURF on lead, took every +2Lv trainer with a counter-typed healthy lead. Map 0 trainers are single-Pokemon and safe if you out-type them.

Catches raise your LEVELS too, not just body count: drafting Lv8-10 catches through map 1 lifted my whole team toward the +2Lv-trainer threshold without fighting anything. Prefer the highest-level catch offered over wild XP every time.

Tutors stack within a run: Kanto maps 0-2 offered multiple tutors and I upgraded twice (Bubble→Surf→Hydro Pump on one carry). Always take every reachable tutor; put each upgrade on your strongest STAB carry.

Kanto map 0 repeatable clean route (2 runs, zero faints): catch->catch->+2Lv trainer->tutor(Surf on carry)->safe wild->second tutor(EQ on 2nd carry)->pokecenter->gym. 3 bodies + double tutor + full-HP boss = badge 1 every time.
Evolution EXISTS in Pokelike (run1 Squirtle became Wartortle ~Lv16). Eviolite (+50% DEF/SpD) BLOCKS evolution — great short-term bulk on a lead/carry, but permanent evo lock; weigh before equipping.

CAUTION: after using Rare Candy (Lv12→13) my lead Squirtle showed 0/34 with NO battle logged — either candies can zero HP or level-up HP recalc bugged. Check team HP after ANY consumable; never assume an item turn was free.
Kanto map 1 layout: pokecenter at layer 7 sits right before the gym (layer 8), same as map 0; trade nodes ($) appear at layers 4 and 6 — scout what they offer before committing.
runs.plan: Kanto map 1 (badge 2): team is Squirtle Lv12+Specs lead, Mankey Lv11, Goldeen Lv11. Kanto map1 Fisherman (+2Lv Water): full-HP Lv11 Exeggcute RESISTING Water and hitting SE Grass still FAINTED, and the chain killed Psyduck + Rhyhorn too — 3 bodies in one node. +2Lv trainers are run-enders regardless of typing; only enter one if a pokecenter is reachable within 1-2 layers after, and expect to lose the lead even when the matchup is perfect.

Map-1 wilds can kill THREE bodies in ONE node (run 12): full-HP Lv13 Kabuto (Rock/Water, bulkiest body) led and fainted, then Squirtle + Magnemite chained behind it. NO lead survives a map-1 wild, not even a bulky STAB counter. Never enter any map-1 battle node unless the layer has nothing else; if forced, expect to lose the lead and 1-2 more bodies.

Kanto map-0 wilds are NOT free XP either: run 11, full-HP Lv6 STAB Bubble+Expert Belt Squirtle dropped to 3/21 on a single +1Lv map-0 wild. No wild anywhere is safe; only enter one with an expendable body leading and healthy backup behind.

Check team HP on the map screen IMMEDIATELY after every battle node: run 12's single wild left 3 of 6 bodies at 0HP. If any body shows 0HP, route to a pokecenter before anything else — the layer-7 pokecenter before Kanto map-1 gym saved that run.
runs.plan: Kanto map 1 (notes 10/11/18/29/30/31): battles are lethal here — wilds have killed two full-HP bodies in one node and +2Lv trainers faint perfect-counter leads. Route: catch nodes through the early layers (bodies + free levels), prefer ? / item / tutor / trade nodes over ANY battle; take the layer-5 item (Sacred Ash has appeared there before), trade any offer (+3 levels, zero risk), pokecenter at layer 7 before the gym at layer 8. Scout the gym tooltip the moment it's visible and lead the typed counter at FULL HP. Only enter a trainer if nothing else exists on the layer AND a pokecenter is reachable within 1-2 layers after.

notebook: Kanto run 1: drafted Squirtle (best bulk: 19/11/11, Bubble Water STAB). Charmander looked like the trap pick; Fire is bad early in Kanto.

Kanto map 0: Officer/Firebreather trainers = Fire Pokemon, Water STAB lead walks them. Pokecenter at layer 7 sits right before the gym: take it if lead under ~80% HP. Items do NOT carry between runs — only notes do; re-equip each run.

Red Card does NOT save a badly disadvantaged lead: Kanto map 1 Scientist (Electric/Poison) one-shot my Lv16 Wartortle from full HP. Never let a weak-to-type Pokemon lead a trainer fight — swap lead first, it's free.
Read the gym leader's tooltip as soon as its node is visible — never enter an unscouted gym. Plan the counter-lead several layers ahead so you arrive with the right type and full HP.

Resist ≠ safe: Lv8 Voltorb (Electric, resists Electric) fainted to a +2 Levels Scientist on Kanto map 0. Don't lead an underlevelled mono-resist into a +2 Levels trainer; lead the healthy STAB carry instead.

Move tutor tier upgrades are huge: Bubble→SURF(80), Bulldoze→EARTHQUAKE(100) roughly doubled damage. Take the tutor whenever reachable. Expert Belt on an SE-hitting STAB carry (Squirtle vs Fire map) cleared Kanto map 0 losing zero HP.

Wild battles are NOT free XP: my full-HP Lv22 Krabby fainted to a Kanto map-2 wild node. Check the wild's likely type before leading; never assume a battle node is safe just because it says "+1 level".

Kanto run 2 draft worked well: 5 bodies by map 0's end (catches cost turns, not HP); coverage core = Water lead + Electric + Fighting + Ground/Rock + bulky Water backup. Choice Scarf on the fastest STAB carry = guaranteed first strike every battle, best early item.

Kanto map1 Scientist (+2Lv, Elec/Poison) killed BOTH my leads: Lv10 Geodude was ELECTRIC-IMMUNE and still fainted, then backup died too. Immunity/resist does not protect an underlevelled lead — arrive at +2Lv trainers Lv13+, or skip them entirely.

Map-1 wilds are NOT free XP: they've killed a FULL-HP Surf Squirtle twice AND a full-HP Lv9 Kabuto (run 8). No lead is safe there — treat every map-1 wild as costing a body's worth of HP or worse. Skip wilds whenever a catch/item/question/trade node exists; if forced, lead the most expendable body with healthy backup.

+2Lv trainers faint even perfect leads: Kanto map1-2 Bug Catchers killed Lv13 AND Lv15 Flying-STAB leads; map1 Firebreather fainted my Lv13 Surf-STAB Squirtle (super-effective, still died). Enter +2Lv fights expecting to lose the lead's HP or the body; heal immediately after, never enter one with your only healthy carry.

Kanto map 0 cleared to badge 1, zero faints: 3 bodies (Squirtle/Seel/Drowzee), tutor SURF on lead, took every +2Lv trainer with a counter-typed healthy lead. Map 0 trainers are single-Pokemon and safe if you out-type them.

Catches raise your LEVELS too, not just body count: drafting Lv8-10 catches through map 1 lifted my whole team toward the +2Lv-trainer threshold without fighting anything. Prefer the highest-level catch offered over wild XP every time.

Tutors stack within a run: Kanto maps 0-2 offered multiple tutors and I upgraded twice (Bubble→Surf→Hydro Pump on one carry). Always take every reachable tutor; put each upgrade on your strongest STAB carry.

Kanto map 0 clean route (2 runs zero faints): catch->catch->tutor(Surf)->second tutor(EQ)->pokecenter->gym, skipping ALL battles. REVISED run 11: the 'safe wild' step nearly killed my lead (full->3/21) — map-0 wilds are not safe either; skip every battle node on map 0 too.
Evolution EXISTS in Pokelike (run1 Squirtle became Wartortle ~Lv16). Eviolite (+50% DEF/SpD) BLOCKS evolution — great short-term bulk on a lead/carry, but permanent evo lock; weigh before equipping.

Rare Candy HP bug is INTERMITTENT: run 11 candy left lead at full HP, but an earlier run showed 0/34 after a candy with no battle logged. Still check team HP after ANY consumable; if a body shows 0HP, heal or swap lead before any battle node (chain-wipe risk, note 24).

Map-1 wilds can kill THREE bodies in ONE node (run 12): full-HP Lv13 Kabuto (Rock/Water, bulkiest body) led and fainted, then Squirtle + Magnemite chained behind it. NO lead survives a map-1 wild, not even a bulky STAB counter. Never enter any map-1 battle node unless the layer has nothing else; if forced, expect to lose the lead and 1-2 more bodies.

Kanto map-0 wilds are NOT free XP either: run 11, full-HP Lv6 STAB Bubble+Expert Belt Squirtle dropped to 3/21 on a single +1Lv map-0 wild. No wild anywhere is safe; only enter one with an expendable body leading and healthy backup behind.

Check team HP on the map screen IMMEDIATELY after every battle node: run 12's single wild left 3 of 6 bodies at 0HP. If any body shows 0HP, route to a pokecenter before anything else — the layer-7 pokecenter before Kanto map-1 gym saved that run.
Moon Stone = USABLE force-evolution kept in BAG, works at any level (run 13, map 0): evolve the lead carry for a permanent stat jump; check HP after any consumable (note 17 bug risk).
Trades FAIL silently when your team is FULL (6/6): run 14 map-1 trade node consumed the turn, no swap screen appeared, body unchanged. Only enter a trade with an open slot, or expect nothing.
Call set_lead in its OWN turn and wait for "ok", then play(): batching them in one block can fail silently (run 15 step 4) and the intended lead sat behind while Squirtle tanked a wild to half HP.
Trades give +3 LEVELS but never heal: run 16 trade lifted fainted Drowzee Lv8->Lv11 and it stayed 0/34. Don't count a trade as recovery for a fainted body.

notebook: Kanto run 1: drafted Squirtle (best bulk: 19/11/11, Bubble Water STAB). Charmander looked like the trap pick; Fire is bad early in Kanto.

Kanto map 0: Officer/Firebreather trainers = Fire Pokemon, Water STAB lead walks them. Pokecenter at layer 7 sits right before the gym: take it if lead under ~80% HP. Items do NOT carry between runs — only notes do; re-equip each run.

Red Card does NOT save a badly disadvantaged lead: Kanto map 1 Scientist (Electric/Poison) one-shot my Lv16 Wartortle from full HP. Never let a weak-to-type Pokemon lead a trainer fight — swap lead first, it's free.
Read the gym leader's tooltip as soon as its node is visible — never enter an unscouted gym. Plan the counter-lead several layers ahead so you arrive with the right type and full HP.

Resist ≠ safe: Lv8 Voltorb (Electric, resists Electric) fainted to a +2 Levels Scientist on Kanto map 0. Don't lead an underlevelled mono-resist into a +2 Levels trainer; lead the healthy STAB carry instead.

Move tutor tier upgrades are huge: Bubble→SURF(80), Bulldoze→EARTHQUAKE(100) roughly doubled damage. Take the tutor whenever reachable. Expert Belt on an SE-hitting STAB carry (Squirtle vs Fire map) cleared Kanto map 0 losing zero HP.

Wild battles are NOT free XP: my full-HP Lv22 Krabby fainted to a Kanto map-2 wild node. Check the wild's likely type before leading; never assume a battle node is safe just because it says "+1 level".

Kanto run 2 draft worked well: 5 bodies by map 0's end (catches cost turns, not HP); coverage core = Water lead + Electric + Fighting + Ground/Rock + bulky Water backup. Choice Scarf on the fastest STAB carry = guaranteed first strike every battle, best early item.

Kanto map1 Scientist (+2Lv, Elec/Poison) killed BOTH my leads: Lv10 Geodude was ELECTRIC-IMMUNE and still fainted, then backup died too. Immunity/resist does not protect an underlevelled lead — arrive at +2Lv trainers Lv13+, or skip them entirely.

Map-1 wilds are NOT free XP: they've killed a FULL-HP Surf Squirtle twice AND a full-HP Lv9 Kabuto (run 8). No lead is safe there — treat every map-1 wild as costing a body's worth of HP or worse. Skip wilds whenever a catch/item/question/trade node exists; if forced, lead the most expendable body with healthy backup.

+2Lv trainers faint even perfect leads: Kanto map1-2 Bug Catchers killed Lv13 AND Lv15 Flying-STAB leads; map1 Firebreather fainted my Lv13 Surf-STAB Squirtle (super-effective, still died). Enter +2Lv fights expecting to lose the lead's HP or the body; heal immediately after, never enter one with your only healthy carry.

Kanto map 0 cleared to badge 1, zero faints: 3 bodies (Squirtle/Seel/Drowzee), tutor SURF on lead, took every +2Lv trainer with a counter-typed healthy lead. Map 0 trainers are single-Pokemon and safe if you out-type them.

Catches raise your LEVELS too, not just body count: drafting Lv8-10 catches through map 1 lifted my whole team toward the +2Lv-trainer threshold without fighting anything. Prefer the highest-level catch offered over wild XP every time.

Tutors stack within a run: Kanto maps 0-2 offered multiple tutors and I upgraded twice (Bubble→Surf→Hydro Pump on one carry). Always take every reachable tutor; put each upgrade on your strongest STAB carry.

Kanto map 0 clean route (2 runs zero faints): catch->catch->tutor(Surf)->second tutor(EQ)->pokecenter->gym, skipping ALL battles. REVISED run 11: the 'safe wild' step nearly killed my lead (full->3/21) — map-0 wilds are not safe either; skip every battle node on map 0 too.
Evolution EXISTS in Pokelike (run1 Squirtle became Wartortle ~Lv16). Eviolite (+50% DEF/SpD) BLOCKS evolution — great short-term bulk on a lead/carry, but permanent evo lock; weigh before equipping.

Rare Candy HP bug is INTERMITTENT: run 11 candy left lead at full HP, but an earlier run showed 0/34 after a candy with no battle logged. Still check team HP after ANY consumable; if a body shows 0HP, heal or swap lead before any battle node (chain-wipe risk, note 24).
